title: Tell the truth, and how
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When did you last hold back a true thing because it might hurt?

There are two paths, Jose said. You can tell people the truth, because deep down you want them to get better, and it bothers you as a leader that you are cheating them from reaching their full potential. But your delivery may not be how they want to receive it.
He said the person in the book probably only knows one way to communicate harshly. He suggested the film Whiplash as a must-watch, and that he watched it with his children.

A student said: the nobility is in the truth. A student asked: is there a balance between the two extremes? People are so sensitive today. How can I stop hurting their feelings? Jose said: there is always a balance.
It is not only how you express an honest opinion to others, Jose said. How do you talk to yourself? We know how to cushion ourselves and justify: I'm doing well, I'm happy with my progress.
How many of us are comfortable saying: I'm thirty years old, I'm not where I want to be, I don't have freedom of time. What am I doing wrong? And not only about numbers: why wasn't it more?

A student said: how you speak to yourself internally is very reflective of how you guide and criticize others. Use the golden rule: how would I want to be guided? Saying something is bad isn't constructive. Explain why. Give more words than that.
A student said harsh feedback is motivating but doesn't help people develop the self-discipline to chase the goals.
Jose said there is a difference between lack of discipline, which is will, and sheer lack of ability. A person with the will but not the ability is coachable. A student agreed.

With children, he said, never say: you're so good at that. The right comment is: you worked so hard to get where you are. Celebrate the process. A student said: appreciating the effort, not the result.
What would you say if you spoke to yourself as you would to someone you lead?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one true thing you have held back from someone you lead.
Write how you would say it so they can hear it.
Write what you tell yourself about your progress and what is a cushion.
Write the difference between will and ability on your team.
Write the effort you will praise this week.

check.q: What did a student say is in the truth?
What did Jose say you should say to a child who wins?
choices: You worked so hard to get where you are

check.q: How did a student describe a person with the will but not the ability?

recap: Tell the truth, with words that help. Praise the effort. Talk to yourself honestly.
